stories.title: India notifies first tariff cuts under New Zealand FTA
stories.summary: From 20 October, India will apply customs‑duty concessions on selected New Zealand imports under the bilateral agreement. Sheep meat will be charged zero basic customs duty, while fish, wine and manuka honey will receive specific duty rates, and kiwi fruit will be taxed at 15 percent. Dairy products are excluded from the concessions.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.
stories.change: New high-signal event entered the brief.

stories.title: Trump suspends pending Russia sanctions amid dispute with Ukraine
stories.summary: President Donald Trump issued an executive order on Friday night that suspended a number of Russia sanctions scheduled to take effect in two days. The sanctions had been passed by Congress and signed into law in September. The move drew criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who said the United States was disregarding the measures, and prompted backlash from US lawmakers. The suspension follows a recent controversial U.S. agreement to import Russian diesel and Ukrainian accusations that key military support has been withdrawn.
stories.why: The suspension reduces U.S. pressure on Russia and strains U.S.-Ukraine coordination on security and energy matters.
stories.previousTitle: Trump suspends Russia sanctions days before they take effect amid dispute with Zelensky
stories.previousSummary: On Friday night President Donald Trump issued an executive order suspending a group of Russia sanctions that Congress had passed and he had signed into law, delaying them by two days before they were scheduled to become effective. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the action as a disregard for the sanctions. The move comes as relations between Washington and Kyiv have soured following a U.S. deal to import Russian diesel and Kyiv’s claim that the administration has cut key military support.
stories.change: No material change since the previous brief.

stories.title: Trump waives 100% tariffs on Russian oil, GTRI says relief for India is temporary
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced a waiver of the previously threatened 100% tariffs on Russian oil purchases. The Global Trade and Investment (GTRI) think tank warned that the relief is only temporary because Washington could reinstate the duties at any time. GTRI cited U.S. purchases of Russian diesel, tariff protection for China, and ongoing India‑U.S. trade talks as possible reasons for the move and urged New Delhi to protect its energy security.
stories.why: India needs to factor the provisional nature of the tariff waiver into its energy‑import strategy and trade negotiations.
stories.previousTitle: Trump waives 100% tariff on Russian oil, offering India temporary relief
stories.previousSummary: The United States announced a waiver of the threatened 100% tariff on Russian oil for buyers, including India. GTRI warned the relief is temporary and duties could be reinstated, citing U.S. purchases of Russian diesel, tariff protection for China, and ongoing India‑U.S. trade talks as possible reasons. The think‑tank urged New Delhi to protect its energy security and avoid permanent trade concessions.
stories.change: No material change since the previous brief.
